title: The AI boom could change where interest rates end up, a top central banker says
key_facts: Uchida spoke in Tokyo on Monday 5 Oct 2026
He called AI "a big positive demand shock" that has put upward pressure on the economy and prices
AI could also lift supply by raising productivity and capital stock
This could affect r-star, the neutral rate of interest
If the neutral rate rises, central banks may need to keep rates higher than investors expected
10-year JGB yield about 3.09% midday Monday, near a three-decade high; 30-year touched a record 4.235%
ING strategists said last week that AI could account for about one-fifth of the recent rise in long-term yields
quote_evidence: "First, it is a big positive demand shock, which has put upward pressure on the economy and prices."
On Monday, the benchmark 10-year JGB yield stood at 3.09% around midday in Japan, hovering near a three-decade high.
why_it_matters_hint: If AI lifts the neutral rate, higher borrowing costs could last longer.
notes: Same speech as C07-04. Business Insider also cites ING strategists (last week) saying AI could account for roughly one-fifth of the recent rise in long-term bond yields.
